name: Shorbet Kharshouf (Egyptian Artichoke Soup)

ingredients.name: frozen artichoke hearts, slightly thawed and coarsely chopped
fresh lemon juice, from 1 lemon divided
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions.primary_message: In a medium saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium-low heat until shimmering. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly golden, about 7 minutes. Add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add artichoke hearts and cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through and beginning to soften, about 2 minutes. Add vegetable broth and 1 tablespoon lemon juice and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook until artichokes are very tender, 12 to 15 minutes.

Remove soup from heat. Using an immersion blender, blend until smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer soup to a blender and blend until smooth. (When blending hot liquids, work in batches if needed to avoid overfilling the blender, hold the lid down with a kitchen towel, start the blender on low, and slowly bring it up to high speed.) Season with pepper to taste and stir in remaining 1/2 tablespoon lemon juice. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer for a smoother consistency, if desired.
Ladle soup into bowls and drizzle with olive oil. Top with parsley, followed by pita chips and a single anchovy fillet, if using. Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

description: Frozen artichoke hearts make this easy Egyptian soup a breeze to prepare. It gets bright flavor from plenty of lemon and a silky, creamy texture from blending—no dairy needed.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Pita chips (optional); see notes; 4 anchovies fillets (optional)

Optional substitutions: homemade vegetable stock → store-bought low-sodium vegetable broth

Notes: You can use store-bought pita chips or make homemade ones using the recipe that accompanies our shorabet adas recipe.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Nermine Mansour
